findings.reason: the dependency is the one the section's whole mechanism rests on, and recording it costs one metadata edit.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` gives s16 `["a-run-has-one-live-worker#s15"]` only, although §16 opens by superseding §13's "first launch under a fresh run id takes no reservation" and rewrites the functions §13 landed; a reader of the graph sees no edge to the section it modifies

findings.reason: the node's gate is scored on a base-failing control per behaviour change, and a case that cannot fail at the base would be reported as a missing control unless the done-when relabels it.
findings.text: the case "an in-harness launch takes no reservation" is listed among the behaviour changes that must "fail at the dispatch base and pass at the head", but §16 keeps §13's in-harness exemption unchanged (`refuse_held_launch`, dispatch.py:2873), so that case passes at the base and is a regression case the done-when does not name as one

findings.reason: they already answer None in production today because `claim_next_attempt` has no production caller, so removing them changes no behaviour and the conditional "if no other reader of it remains" already covers the path.
findings.text: §16 says the claim pair's removal leaves one dead reader and deletes it with its branch, but `_attempt_claim_seconds` (reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:625) and `_attempt_started_from_claim` (:651) also read `attempt-N.claim` through `resumption.attempt_claim_path`, which has production callers via `_attempt_started_seconds`; after the pair is deleted those readers keep a live path that can only ever return None

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — each cited symbol and line resolves at HEAD (`launch_reservation_key` dispatch_launch.py:2218, `held_launch_reservation`:2318, `reserve_launch_attempt`:2384, `refuse_held_launch`:2445, `_record_reservation_supervisor` is the import alias at dispatch.py:2855, `claim_next_attempt`/`release_attempt_claim` resumption.py:389/358, `_newest_attempt_claim_number` recovery_liveness.py:614, the two claim tests at test_a_resume_never_launches_beside_another_node.py:344/368, the vacuous `pid > 0` cases at test_a_concurrent_launch_is_refused.py:446/461 and `test_a_fresh_run_id_takes_no_reservation`:776).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §16's done-when puts "an in-harness launch takes no reservation" under "each behaviour change has a case that fails at the dispatch base and passes at the head", but that behaviour is §13's and is unchanged, so no base-failing control exists for it.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate log and the negative-control log are named under the run directory, with revision, literal command and a bare EXIT= line, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the one renamed symbol states the rule it now asserts, and no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol, file or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §16 removes one dead claim reader (`_newest_attempt_claim_number`) but leaves its sibling `_attempt_claim_seconds`/`_attempt_started_from_claim` reading the same `attempt-N.claim` files, so `attempt_claim_path` keeps a live caller and a reader that must always answer None.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the section names one mechanism, the launch reservation's lifecycle, and the test repairs it lists are the tests that pin that mechanism.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §16's `plan-section-depends-on` entry names only `#s15`, but the section supersedes §13's fresh-run rule and edits the reservation functions §13 landed (`reserve_launch_attempt`, `held_launch_reservation`, `launch_reservation_key`), so its upstream `#s13` is undeclared.
